finding.claim: The /logo handler fetches a user-supplied URL after only a substring check (strings.Contains(raw, "example.io")). The check is bypassable, for example with http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/?x=example.io, http://example.io@127.0.0.1:8081/ or http://attacker.tld/example.io. The default http.Get client follows redirects, and the response body is copied back to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF to internal hosts and cloud metadata.
finding.source: r.FormValue("logo") at main.go:31, an unauthenticated HTTP request parameter on the public :8081 listener (main.go:42-44)
finding.sink: http.Get(raw) at main.go:36, with the response streamed back via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:38

trace.note: raw := r.FormValue("logo"), attacker-controlled query or form value
strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") is a substring check. It does not parse the URL or compare the hostname, so any URL containing the string passes.
http.Get(raw) uses http.DefaultClient, which follows redirects with no per-hop validation and no scheme restriction
the response body is returned to the attacker, so the SSRF is non-blind

finding.guards_checked: The only guard is the substring check at main.go:32, which does not close the finding. There is no URL parsing, no .hostname strict set membership, no scheme restriction, no CheckRedirect and no IP or CIDR egress filtering. No authentication on the route. Severity is HIGH: no auth, response returned, and redirects followed.

verdict.guard_found: Only a substring check strings.Contains(raw, "example.io") at main.go:32. It does not close the finding. No URL parsing, no host membership, no scheme restriction, and no CheckRedirect on the default client. The strict trusted-host map is used only in the separate /cdn handler (main.go:20).
verdict.reason: main.go:31 takes an unauthenticated form value, main.go:32 only does a substring check, and main.go:36 passes it to http.Get (default client, follows redirects) with the body returned at main.go:38, so SSRF is confirmed.
